Human: Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Snake game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- include/Types.h is the sole definition site for Position and Direction; every header that mentions either type must include "Types.h" directly
- include/IRandom.h declares both IRandom and DefaultRandom; src/Random.cpp must include "IRandom.h" exactly and must never include or refer to a nonexistent Random.h
- include/IRandom.h must directly include <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random>; spell size types std::size_t and seed types std::uint32_t because std::mt19937 is a declared data member
- include/Game.h must directly include "Board.h", "IRandom.h", "Snake.h", and "Types.h" plus <cstddef>, <deque>, and <optional>; forward declarations and transitive includes are forbidden for these dependencies
- in both Full API specification and Logic Analysis, the include/IRandom.h entry must literally enumerate \`#include <cstddef>\`, \`#include <cstdint>\`, and \`#include <random>\`, and the include/Game.h entry must literally enumerate \`#include "Board.h"\`, \`#include "IRandom.h"\`, \`#include "Snake.h"\`, \`#include "Types.h"\`, \`#include <cstddef>\`, \`#include <deque>\`, and \`#include <optional>\`
- every header must directly include every standard type it declares, including <deque>, <optional>, <set>, or <vector> when used; do not rely on transitive includes
- Game must construct its non-default-constructible Snake member in the constructor initializer list; do not default-construct and later assign it
- use the exact collision-query signature bool wouldSelfCollide(const Position& next, bool grow) const (or omit that helper entirely); no function may refer to a grow variable that is absent from its parameters or local declarations
- specify an exact Game constructor initializer containing snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3); constructor-body assignment is forbidden, and dimensions must be validated before any game tick
- each target_compile_options flag in CMake must be a separate list argument, never one quoted string containing multiple flags
- repeat these exact filename, literal include-line, collision-signature, constructor-initializer, and CMake rules in the Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; a generic statement that headers are self-contained is insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 31 functions or methods
- about 590 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- grid-based snake movement
- direction rules that reject immediate reversal
- food placement and consumption
- growth and score updates
- wall and self collision
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Snake game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- include/Types.h is the sole definition site for Position and Direction; every header that mentions either type must include "Types.h" directly
- include/IRandom.h declares both IRandom and DefaultRandom; src/Random.cpp must include "IRandom.h" exactly and must never include or refer to a nonexistent Random.h
- include/IRandom.h must directly include <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random>; spell size types std::size_t and seed types std::uint32_t because std::mt19937 is a declared data member
- include/Game.h must directly include "Board.h", "IRandom.h", "Snake.h", and "Types.h" plus <cstddef>, <deque>, and <optional>; forward declarations and transitive includes are forbidden for these dependencies
- in both Full API specification and Logic Analysis, the include/IRandom.h entry must literally enumerate \`#include <cstddef>\`, \`#include <cstdint>\`, and \`#include <random>\`, and the include/Game.h entry must literally enumerate \`#include "Board.h"\`, \`#include "IRandom.h"\`, \`#include "Snake.h"\`, \`#include "Types.h"\`, \`#include <cstddef>\`, \`#include <deque>\`, and \`#include <optional>\`
- every header must directly include every standard type it declares, including <deque>, <optional>, <set>, or <vector> when used; do not rely on transitive includes
- Game must construct its non-default-constructible Snake member in the constructor initializer list; do not default-construct and later assign it
- use the exact collision-query signature bool wouldSelfCollide(const Position& next, bool grow) const (or omit that helper entirely); no function may refer to a grow variable that is absent from its parameters or local declarations
- specify an exact Game constructor initializer containing snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3); constructor-body assignment is forbidden, and dimensions must be validated before any game tick
- each target_compile_options flag in CMake must be a separate list argument, never one quoted string containing multiple flags
- repeat these exact filename, literal include-line, collision-signature, constructor-initializer, and CMake rules in the Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; a generic statement that headers are self-contained is insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 31 functions or methods
- about 590 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- grid-based snake movement
- direction rules that reject immediate reversal
- food placement and consumption
- growth and score updates
- wall and self collision
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- include/Types.h is the sole definition site for Position and Direction; every header that mentions either type must include "Types.h" directly
- include/IRandom.h declares both IRandom and DefaultRandom; src/Random.cpp must include "IRandom.h" exactly and must never include or refer to a nonexistent Random.h
- include/IRandom.h must directly include <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random>; spell size types std::size_t and seed types std::uint32_t because std::mt19937 is a declared data member
- include/Game.h must directly include "Board.h", "IRandom.h", "Snake.h", and "Types.h" plus <cstddef>, <deque>, and <optional>; forward declarations and transitive includes are forbidden for these dependencies
- in both Full API specification and Logic Analysis, the include/IRandom.h entry must literally enumerate \`#include <cstddef>\`, \`#include <cstdint>\`, and \`#include <random>\`, and the include/Game.h entry must literally enumerate \`#include "Board.h"\`, \`#include "IRandom.h"\`, \`#include "Snake.h"\`, \`#include "Types.h"\`, \`#include <cstddef>\`, \`#include <deque>\`, and \`#include <optional>\`
- every header must directly include every standard type it declares, including <deque>, <optional>, <set>, or <vector> when used; do not rely on transitive includes
- Game must construct its non-default-constructible Snake member in the constructor initializer list; do not default-construct and later assign it
- use the exact collision-query signature bool wouldSelfCollide(const Position& next, bool grow) const (or omit that helper entirely); no function may refer to a grow variable that is absent from its parameters or local declarations
- specify an exact Game constructor initializer containing snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3); constructor-body assignment is forbidden, and dimensions must be validated before any game tick
- each target_compile_options flag in CMake must be a separate list argument, never one quoted string containing multiple flags
- repeat these exact filename, literal include-line, collision-signature, constructor-initializer, and CMake rules in the Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; a generic statement that headers are self-contained is insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 31 functions or methods
- about 590 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- grid-based snake movement
- direction rules that reject immediate reversal
- food placement and consumption
- growth and score updates
- wall and self collision
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Header includes <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random> and uses std::size_t, std::uint32_t, std::mt19937.\\n\\ninclude/Board.h:\\n- class Board { public: Board(std::size_t width, std::size_t height); std::size_t getWidth() const noexcept; std::size_t getHeight() const noexcept; bool inBounds(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::size_t width_; std::size_t height_; };\\nSemantics: Stores immutable grid dimensions. inBounds returns true iff 0 <= p.x < width and 0 <= p.y < height.\\n\\ninclude/Snake.h:\\n- class Snake { public: Snake(Position start, Direction dir, int initialLength); Position head() const; Position tail() const; const std::deque<Position>& body() const noexcept; Direction direction() const noexcept; bool trySetDirection(Direction d); void advanceTo(Position next, bool grow); bool occupies(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::deque<Position> body_; Direction dir_; };\\nSemantics: Constructor initializes a length-3 body when called by Game as per protocol, extending opposite to initial direction. trySetDirection prevents 180-degree reversal relative to current direction; returns true if accepted, false if ignored. advanceTo moves head to 'next'; if grow is false, it pops the tail; if grow is true, it keeps the tail (growing by one). occupies checks if any segment equals p.\\n\\ninclude/Game.h:\\n- class Game { public: Game(std::size_t width, std::size_t height, IRandom& rng); void reset(); void setDirection(Direction d); void tick(); bool isGameOver() const noexcept; std::size_t getScore() const noexcept; const Snake& getSnake() const noexcept; std::optional<Position> getFood() const; private: void placeFood(); bool wouldSelfCollide(Position next, bool grow) const; private: Board board_; IRandom& rng_; Snake snake_; std::optional<Position> food_; std::size_t score_; bool gameOver_; std::optional<Direction> pendingDir_; };\\nSemantics:\\n- Construction: validates dimensions (both width and height must be > 0; otherwise throws std::invalid_argument). Resets score_=0, gameOver_=false, pendingDir_=std::nullopt, and places initial food on an unoccupied cell using RNG.\\n- setDirection: queues a pending direction; actual change is applied at the start of the next tick via Snake::trySetDirection, preserving reversal-prevention.\\n- tick: if gameOver_ is true, it is a no-op. Moving into the current tail position is allowed only when grow == false (i.e., not eating this tick). If next equals current food position, sets grow=true, advances snake with grow=true, increments score_, and calls placeFood(). Otherwise advances with grow=false. If out-of-bounds or self-collide, sets gameOver_=true and does not move further for this tick.\\n- getFood returns std::nullopt if no food is currently placed (e.g., if board is fully occupied). placeFood selects uniformly among unoccupied cells using rng_.next().\\n\\nsrc/Random.cpp:\\n- Implements DefaultRandom::DefaultRandom(seed) to seed engine_ and DefaultRandom::next(maxExclusive) using uniform_int_distribution in [0, maxExclusive-1]. This header is the sole definition site for both Position and Direction; any header using them must include this header directly.\\n\\ninclude/IRandom.h:\\n- class IRandom { public: virtual ~IRandom() = default; virtual std::size_t next(std::size_t maxExclusive) = 0; };\\n- class DefaultRandom final : public IRandom { public: explicit DefaultRandom(std::uint32_t seed); std::size_t next(std::size_t maxExclusive) override; private: std::mt19937 engine_; };\\nSemantics: next(maxExclusive) returns an integer in [0, maxExclusive) uniformly. Behavior is deterministic given the seed. Header includes <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random> and uses std::size_t, std::uint32_t, std::mt19937.\\n\\ninclude/Board.h:\\n- class Board { public: Board(std::size_t width, std::size_t height); std::size_t getWidth() const noexcept; std::size_t getHeight() const noexcept; bool inBounds(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::size_t width_; std::size_t height_; };\\nSemantics: Stores immutable grid dimensions. inBounds returns true iff 0 <= p.x < width and 0 <= p.y < height.\\n\\ninclude/Snake.h:\\n- class Snake { public: Snake(Position start, Direction dir, int initialLength); Position head() const; Position tail() const; const std::deque<Position>& body() const noexcept; Direction direction() const noexcept; bool trySetDirection(Direction d); void advanceTo(Position next, bool grow); bool occupies(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::deque<Position> body_; Direction dir_; };\\nSemantics: Constructor initializes a length-3 body when called by Game as per protocol, extending opposite to initial direction. trySetDirection prevents 180-degree reversal relative to current direction; returns true if accepted, false if ignored. advanceTo moves head to 'next'; if grow is false, it pops the tail; if grow is true, it keeps the tail (growing by one). occupies checks if any segment equals p.\\n\\ninclude/Game.h:\\n- class Game { public: Game(std::size_t width, std::size_t height, IRandom& rng); void reset(); void setDirection(Direction d); void tick(); bool isGameOver() const noexcept; std::size_t getScore() const noexcept; const Snake& getSnake() const noexcept; std::optional<Position> getFood() const; private: void placeFood(); bool wouldSelfCollide(Position next, bool grow) const; private: Board board_; IRandom& rng_; Snake snake_; std::optional<Position> food_; std::size_t score_; bool gameOver_; std::optional<Direction> pendingDir_; };\\nSemantics:\\n- Construction: validates dimensions (both width and height must be > 0; otherwise throws std::invalid_argument). Initializes the snake exactly as: snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3). Resets score_=0, gameOver_=false, pendingDir_=std::nullopt, and places initial food on an unoccupied cell using RNG.\\n- setDirection: queues a pending direction; actual change is applied at the start of the next tick via Snake::trySetDirection, preserving reversal-prevention.\\n- tick: if gameOver_ is true, it is a no-op. Otherwise, applies pending direction, computes next head based on current direction, checks board_.inBounds(next) and self-collision via wouldSelfCollide(next, grow). Moving into the current tail position is allowed only when grow == false (i.e., not eating this tick). If next equals current food position, sets grow=true, advances snake with grow=true, increments score_, and calls placeFood(). Otherwise advances with grow=false. If out-of-bounds or self-collide, sets gameOver_=true and does not move further for this tick.\\n- getFood returns std::nullopt if no food is currently placed (e.g., if board is fully occupied). placeFood selects uniformly among unoccupied cells using rng_.next().\\n\\nsrc/Random.cpp:\\n- Implements DefaultRandom::DefaultRandom(seed) to seed engine_ and DefaultRandom::next(maxExclusive) using uniform_int_distribution in [0, maxExclusive-1]. Behavior is deterministic given the seed. Header includes <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random> and uses std::size_t, std::uint32_t, std::mt19937.\\n\\ninclude/Board.h:\\n- class Board { public: Board(std::size_t width, std::size_t height); std::size_t getWidth() const noexcept; std::size_t getHeight() const noexcept; bool inBounds(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::size_t width_; std::size_t height_; };\\nSemantics: Stores immutable grid dimensions. inBounds returns true iff 0 <= p.x < width and 0 <= p.y < height.\\n\\ninclude/Snake.h:\\n- class Snake { public: Snake(Position start, Direction dir, int initialLength); Position head() const; Position tail() const; const std::deque<Position>& body() const noexcept; Direction direction() const noexcept; bool trySetDirection(Direction d); void advanceTo(Position next, bool grow); bool occupies(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::deque<Position> body_; Direction dir_; };\\nSemantics: Constructor initializes a length-3 body when called by Game as per protocol, extending opposite to initial direction. trySetDirection prevents 180-degree reversal relative to current direction; returns true if accepted, false if ignored. advanceTo moves head to 'next'; if grow is false, it pops the tail; if grow is true, it keeps the tail (growing by one). occupies checks if any segment equals p.\\n\\ninclude/Game.h:\\n- class Game { public: Game(std::size_t width, std::size_t height, IRandom& rng); void reset(); void setDirection(Direction d); void tick(); bool isGameOver() const noexcept; std::size_t getScore() const noexcept; const Snake& getSnake() const noexcept; std::optional<Position> getFood() const; private: void placeFood(); bool wouldSelfCollide(Position next, bool grow) const; private: Board board_; IRandom& rng_; Snake snake_; std::optional<Position> food_; std::size_t score_; bool gameOver_; std::optional<Direction> pendingDir_; };\\nSemantics:\\n- Construction: validates dimensions (both width and height must be > 0; otherwise throws std::invalid_argument). Resets score_=0, gameOver_=false, pendingDir_=std::nullopt, and places initial food on an unoccupied cell using RNG.\\n- setDirection: queues a pending direction; actual change is applied at the start of the next tick via Snake::trySetDirection, preserving reversal-prevention.\\n- tick: if gameOver_ is true, it is a no-op. Otherwise, applies pending direction, computes next head based on current direction, checks board_.inBounds(next) and self-collision via wouldSelfCollide(next, grow). Moving into the current tail position is allowed only when grow == false (i.e., not eating this tick). If next equals current food position, sets grow=true, advances snake with grow=true, increments score_, and calls placeFood(). Otherwise advances with grow=false. If out-of-bounds or self-collide, sets gameOver_=true and does not move further for this tick.\\n- getFood returns std::nullopt if no food is currently placed (e.g., if board is fully occupied). placeFood selects uniformly among unoccupied cells using rng_.next().\\n\\nsrc/Random.cpp:\\n- Implements DefaultRandom::DefaultRandom(seed) to seed engine_ and DefaultRandom::next(maxExclusive) using uniform_int_distribution in [0, maxExclusive-1]. - struct Position { int x; int y; };
- enum class Direction { Up, Down, Left, Right };
Semantics: Position uses integer grid coordinates. Direction enumerates movement axes. This header is the sole definition site for both Position and Direction; any header using them must include this header directly.

include/IRandom.h:
- class IRandom { public: virtual ~IRandom() = default; virtual std::size_t next(std::size_t maxExclusive) = 0; };
- class DefaultRandom final : public IRandom { public: explicit DefaultRandom(std::uint32_t seed); std::size_t next(std::size_t maxExclusive) override; private: std::mt19937 engine_; };
Semantics: next(maxExclusive) returns an integer in [0, maxExclusive) uniformly. Behavior is deterministic given the seed. Header includes <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random> and uses std::size_t, std::uint32_t, std::mt19937.

include/Board.h:
- class Board { public: Board(std::size_t width, std::size_t height); std::size_t getWidth() const noexcept; std::size_t getHeight() const noexcept; bool inBounds(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::size_t width_; std::size_t height_; };
Semantics: Stores immutable grid dimensions. inBounds returns true iff 0 <= p.x < width and 0 <= p.y < height.

include/Snake.h:
- class Snake { public: Snake(Position start, Direction dir, int initialLength); Position head() const; Position tail() const; const std::deque<Position>& body() const noexcept; Direction direction() const noexcept; bool trySetDirection(Direction d); void advanceTo(Position next, bool grow); bool occupies(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::deque<Position> body_; Direction dir_; };
Semantics: Constructor initializes a length-3 body when called by Game as per protocol, extending opposite to initial direction. trySetDirection prevents 180-degree reversal relative to current direction; returns true if accepted, false if ignored. advanceTo moves head to 'next'; if grow is false, it pops the tail; if grow is true, it keeps the tail (growing by one). occupies checks if any segment equals p.

include/Game.h:
- class Game { public: Game(std::size_t width, std::size_t height, IRandom& rng); void reset(); void setDirection(Direction d); void tick(); bool isGameOver() const noexcept; std::size_t getScore() const noexcept; const Snake& getSnake() const noexcept; std::optional<Position> getFood() const; private: void placeFood(); bool wouldSelfCollide(Position next, bool grow) const; private: Board board_; IRandom& rng_; Snake snake_; std::optional<Position> food_; std::size_t score_; bool gameOver_; std::optional<Direction> pendingDir_; };
Semantics:
- Construction: validates dimensions (both width and height must be > 0; otherwise throws std::invalid_argument). Initializes the snake exactly as: snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3). Resets score_=0, gameOver_=false, pendingDir_=std::nullopt, and places initial food on an unoccupied cell using RNG.
- setDirection: queues a pending direction; actual change is applied at the start of the next tick via Snake::trySetDirection, preserving reversal-prevention.
- tick: if gameOver_ is true, it is a no-op. Otherwise, applies pending direction, computes next head based on current direction, checks board_.inBounds(next) and self-collision via wouldSelfCollide(next, grow). Moving into the current tail position is allowed only when grow == false (i.e., not eating this tick). If next equals current food position, sets grow=true, advances snake with grow=true, increments score_, and calls placeFood(). Otherwise advances with grow=false. If out-of-bounds or self-collide, sets gameOver_=true and does not move further for this tick.
- getFood returns std::nullopt if no food is currently placed (e.g., if board is fully occupied). placeFood selects uniformly among unoccupied cells using rng_.next().

src/Random.cpp:
- Implements DefaultRandom::DefaultRandom(seed) to seed engine_ and DefaultRandom::next(maxExclusive) using uniform_int_distribution in [0, maxExclusive-1]. Includes "IRandom.h" exactly.

src/Board.cpp:
- Implements Board methods; inBounds uses Position from include/Types.h (via include in include/Board.h).

src/Snake.cpp:
- Implements Snake, including reversal prevention in trySetDirection and growth-safe advanceTo.

src/Game.cpp:
- Implements Game: constructor performs validation, initializes snake_ exactly as specified, places food deterministically using rng_ over unoccupied cells, and ensures movement rules including the 'move into tail allowed only if not growing' rule via wouldSelfCollide.

Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Snake game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- include/Types.h is the sole definition site for Position and Direction; every header that mentions either type must include "Types.h" directly
- include/IRandom.h declares both IRandom and DefaultRandom; src/Random.cpp must include "IRandom.h" exactly and must never include or refer to a nonexistent Random.h
- include/IRandom.h must directly include <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random>; spell size types std::size_t and seed types std::uint32_t because std::mt19937 is a declared data member
- include/Game.h must directly include "Board.h", "IRandom.h", "Snake.h", and "Types.h" plus <cstddef>, <deque>, and <optional>; forward declarations and transitive includes are forbidden for these dependencies
- in both Full API specification and Logic Analysis, the include/IRandom.h entry must literally enumerate \`#include <cstddef>\`, \`#include <cstdint>\`, and \`#include <random>\`, and the include/Game.h entry must literally enumerate \`#include "Board.h"\`, \`#include "IRandom.h"\`, \`#include "Snake.h"\`, \`#include "Types.h"\`, \`#include <cstddef>\`, \`#include <deque>\`, and \`#include <optional>\`
- every header must directly include every standard type it declares, including <deque>, <optional>, <set>, or <vector> when used; do not rely on transitive includes
- Game must construct its non-default-constructible Snake member in the constructor initializer list; do not default-construct and later assign it
- use the exact collision-query signature bool wouldSelfCollide(const Position& next, bool grow) const (or omit that helper entirely); no function may refer to a grow variable that is absent from its parameters or local declarations
- specify an exact Game constructor initializer containing snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3); constructor-body assignment is forbidden, and dimensions must be validated before any game tick
- each target_compile_options flag in CMake must be a separate list argument, never one quoted string containing multiple flags
- repeat these exact filename, literal include-line, collision-signature, constructor-initializer, and CMake rules in the Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; a generic statement that headers are self-contained is insufficient


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 31 functions or methods
- about 590 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- grid-based snake movement
- direction rules that reject immediate reversal
- food placement and consumption
- growth and score updates
- wall and self collision
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

- struct Position { int x; int y; };
- enum class Direction { Up, Down, Left, Right };
Semantics: Position uses integer grid coordinates. Direction enumerates movement axes. This header is the sole definition site for both Position and Direction; any header using them must include this header directly.

include/IRandom.h:
- class IRandom { public: virtual ~IRandom() = default; virtual std::size_t next(std::size_t maxExclusive) = 0; };
- class DefaultRandom final : public IRandom { public: explicit DefaultRandom(std::uint32_t seed); std::size_t next(std::size_t maxExclusive) override; private: std::mt19937 engine_; };
Semantics: next(maxExclusive) returns an integer in [0, maxExclusive) uniformly. Behavior is deterministic given the seed. Header includes <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random> and uses std::size_t, std::uint32_t, std::mt19937.

include/Board.h:
- class Board { public: Board(std::size_t width, std::size_t height); std::size_t getWidth() const noexcept; std::size_t getHeight() const noexcept; bool inBounds(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::size_t width_; std::size_t height_; };
Semantics: Stores immutable grid dimensions. inBounds returns true iff 0 <= p.x < width and 0 <= p.y < height.

include/Snake.h:
- class Snake { public: Snake(Position start, Direction dir, int initialLength); Position head() const; Position tail() const; const std::deque<Position>& body() const noexcept; Direction direction() const noexcept; bool trySetDirection(Direction d); void advanceTo(Position next, bool grow); bool occupies(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::deque<Position> body_; Direction dir_; };
Semantics: Constructor initializes a length-3 body when called by Game as per protocol, extending opposite to initial direction. trySetDirection prevents 180-degree reversal relative to current direction; returns true if accepted, false if ignored. advanceTo moves head to 'next'; if grow is false, it pops the tail; if grow is true, it keeps the tail (growing by one). occupies checks if any segment equals p.

include/Game.h:
- class Game { public: Game(std::size_t width, std::size_t height, IRandom& rng); void reset(); void setDirection(Direction d); void tick(); bool isGameOver() const noexcept; std::size_t getScore() const noexcept; const Snake& getSnake() const noexcept; std::optional<Position> getFood() const; private: void placeFood(); bool wouldSelfCollide(Position next, bool grow) const; private: Board board_; IRandom& rng_; Snake snake_; std::optional<Position> food_; std::size_t score_; bool gameOver_; std::optional<Direction> pendingDir_; };
Semantics:
- Construction: validates dimensions (both width and height must be > 0; otherwise throws std::invalid_argument). Initializes the snake exactly as: snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3). Resets score_=0, gameOver_=false, pendingDir_=std::nullopt, and places initial food on an unoccupied cell using RNG.
- setDirection: queues a pending direction; actual change is applied at the start of the next tick via Snake::trySetDirection, preserving reversal-prevention.
- tick: if gameOver_ is true, it is a no-op. Otherwise, applies pending direction, computes next head based on current direction, checks board_.inBounds(next) and self-collision via wouldSelfCollide(next, grow). Moving into the current tail position is allowed only when grow == false (i.e., not eating this tick). If next equals current food position, sets grow=true, advances snake with grow=true, increments score_, and calls placeFood(). Otherwise advances with grow=false. If out-of-bounds or self-collide, sets gameOver_=true and does not move further for this tick.
- getFood returns std::nullopt if no food is currently placed (e.g., if board is fully occupied). placeFood selects uniformly among unoccupied cells using rng_.next().

src/Random.cpp:
- Implements DefaultRandom::DefaultRandom(seed) to seed engine_ and DefaultRandom::next(maxExclusive) using uniform_int_distribution in [0, maxExclusive-1]. Includes "IRandom.h" exactly.

src/Board.cpp:
- Implements Board methods; inBounds uses Position from include/Types.h (via include in include/Board.h).

src/Snake.cpp:
- Implements Snake, including reversal prevention in trySetDirection and growth-safe advanceTo.

src/Game.cpp:

- struct Position { int x; int y; };
- enum class Direction { Up, Down, Left, Right };
Semantics: Position uses integer grid coordinates. Direction enumerates movement axes. This header is the sole definition site for both Position and Direction; any header using them must include this header directly.

include/IRandom.h:
- class IRandom { public: virtual ~IRandom() = default; virtual std::size_t next(std::size_t maxExclusive) = 0; };
- class DefaultRandom final : public IRandom { public: explicit DefaultRandom(std::uint32_t seed); std::size_t next(std::size_t maxExclusive) override; private: std::mt19937 engine_; };
Semantics: next(maxExclusive) returns an integer in [0, maxExclusive) uniformly. Behavior is deterministic given the seed. Header includes <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random> and uses std::size_t, std::uint32_t, std::mt19937.

include/Board.h:
- class Board { public: Board(std::size_t width, std::size_t height); std::size_t getWidth() const noexcept; std::size_t getHeight() const noexcept; bool inBounds(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::size_t width_; std::size_t height_; };
Semantics: Stores immutable grid dimensions. inBounds returns true iff 0 <= p.x < width and 0 <= p.y < height.

include/Snake.h:
- class Snake { public: Snake(Position start, Direction dir, int initialLength); Position head() const; Position tail() const; const std::deque<Position>& body() const noexcept; Direction direction() const noexcept; bool trySetDirection(Direction d); void advanceTo(Position next, bool grow); bool occupies(Position p) const noexcept; private: std::deque<Position> body_; Direction dir_; };
Semantics: Constructor initializes a length-3 body when called by Game as per protocol, extending opposite to initial direction. trySetDirection prevents 180-degree reversal relative to current direction; returns true if accepted, false if ignored. advanceTo moves head to 'next'; if grow is false, it pops the tail; if grow is true, it keeps the tail (growing by one). occupies checks if any segment equals p.

Semantics:
- Construction: validates dimensions (both width and height must be > 0; otherwise throws std::invalid_argument). Initializes the snake exactly as: snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3). Resets score_=0, gameOver_=false, pendingDir_=std::nullopt, and places initial food on an unoccupied cell using RNG.
- setDirection: queues a pending direction; actual change is applied at the start of the next tick via Snake::trySetDirection, preserving reversal-prevention.
- tick: if gameOver_ is true, it is a no-op. Otherwise, applies pending direction, computes next head based on current direction, checks board_.inBounds(next) and self-collision via wouldSelfCollide(next, grow). Moving into the current tail position is allowed only when grow == false (i.e., not eating this tick). If next equals current food position, sets grow=true, advances snake with grow=true, increments score_, and calls placeFood(). Otherwise advances with grow=false. If out-of-bounds or self-collide, sets gameOver_=true and does not move further for this tick.
- getFood returns std::nullopt if no food is currently placed (e.g., if board is fully occupied). placeFood selects uniformly among unoccupied cells using rng_.next().

- food placement and consumption
- growth and score updates

- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
